text:
The Blackhawks finally beat somebody on Tuesday, 6-3 over a Toronto team on a seven-game skid, and still left the building worried. Connor Bedard left with an upper-body injury, and Mark Lazerus of The Athletic wrote that the team is staring at another Bedard absence. For a rebuild that is built around him, that is the whole story until there's news on how long he is out.

The win had good signs. Frank Nazar and Tyler Bertuzzi scored twice each and Sam Rinzel had three assists, per Lazerus. Rinzel has 10 points in his last 10 games against 4.5 expected, which is a lot of luck on top of real growth, and Nazar has eight. Patrick Kane, back in Chicago, has been part of a Kane, Nazar and Oliver Moore line that takes 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), the best of Jeff Blashill's top units.

Everything else is hard reading. Chicago is 6-13-2 with 43% of the expected goals, 42% at five on five, and has allowed almost ten more goals than its chances against suggest. Both goalies have been more than four goals below expected over their recent starts, and Arvid Soderblom cleared waivers and went to Rockford. The Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pair has been on for 15 goals against and 4 for. Our playoff odds are 1%. The season now is about development, and about Bedard's health.
